_comment: Load-bearing claims only. The audit found 1,197 numeric claims across the base; retrofitting all of them is busywork. These are the ones a live position or a stated conclusion actually rests on -- if one of these is wrong, a decision changes. Every entry carries how it was obtained and how confident I am that it is right, which is NOT the same question. status: verified (I pulled it from the primary source myself) | reported (a secondary source asserts it, I did not verify) | contested (sources disagree and I have not settled it) | unresolved (I flagged it and never closed it).

claims.claim: Nifty FY26 earnings grew 4.5% against 12-15% expected
claims.why_load_bearing: This is the single number that overturned my 'earnings +18%' framing and therefore the entire medium-horizon case. Everything downstream of it changes if it is wrong.
claims.note: The 18% figure was ONE quarter with 60% of the growth from five stocks. The 4.5% is the full-year number.

claims.claim: 4.5% actual versus 6.9% on a reconstituted index
claims.why_load_bearing: Explains WHY Indian consensus misses every year -- survivorship in the index itself. It is the mechanism, not just the observation.

claims.claim: Fed-model ERP has R-squared of 0.5% versus 56.3% for plain P/E
claims.why_load_bearing: Demolished my own ERP chain after I had already given the user three successive ERP numbers. The correction only holds if this holds.
claims.note: Damodaran's rigorous series shows no negative ERP years since 1960, which is a separate and independent check that pointed the same way.

claims.claim: A sub-12-month trade needs ~9.85% more gross return than a 12-month-plus one; 11.8% at high income
claims.obtained: computed in scripts/required_return.py from statutory rates
claims.why_load_bearing: It is the reason the short-horizon sleeve has a higher bar than the medium one. Arithmetic, not opinion.
claims.source: STCG 20% vs LTCG 12.5% + Rs1.25L exemption, Income Tax Act

claims.claim: India -9.9% over 1y and -15.0% over 2y in USD, versus S&P +19.2%
claims.obtained: computed from our own OHLC pulls
claims.why_load_bearing: The rupee is why the local-currency chart flatters the market. Any allocation argument that ignores it is wrong for a global comparison.

claims.claim: India tariff in force is 10% under Section 301(b)/304(a), effective ~2026-07-24, from a 60-country forced-labour investigation initiated 2026-03-12 -- NOT India-specific. ~45% of India's US-bound exports (~$87bn) exempt via Annex I/II. Section 122 Proclamation 11012 bridged from 2026-02-20 (the day IEEPA fell) for its 150-day cap. The 18% came from a bilateral deal under the IEEPA framework struck down nine days later.
claims.obtained: agent research + SCOTUS decision Learning Resources v. Trump, 6-3, 20 Feb 2026
claims.why_load_bearing: I told the user 18% repeatedly. It was wrong. This is the correction and it changes the export-sector maths.
claims.source: 91 FR 47318 doc# 2026-15181 (Sec 301 notice, pub 2026-07-28); 91 FR 47717 doc# 2026-15274 (Presidential Memorandum); 91 FR 9339 doc# 2026-03824 (Proclamation 11012, Sec 122 bridge); 91 FR 18183 doc# 2026-06956 (Proclamation 11020, Sec 232 pharma)
claims.note: Generic pharma is separate: Section 232, 0% from 2026-08-01, 100% Aug 2028, 200% Aug 2029, legally untouched by the IEEPA ruling.

claims.claim: Russia is now >50% of India's crude imports and the discount has narrowed to near-premium
claims.why_load_bearing: Sets the size of the Senate-sanctions tail risk. At >50% it is an index-level risk, not a sector one.

claims.claim: Senate Russia sanctions bill with a 100% tariff threat on India passed 86-11; House pending
claims.why_load_bearing: Largest undated tail risk in the book. The 86-11 margin is the part that matters -- it is veto-proof in that chamber.

claims.claim: SIP and DII flows were double-counted, understating the supply problem by 40%; absorption is 2.15 years at the DII run-rate
claims.obtained: own correction after catching the double-count
claims.why_load_bearing: The supply-absorption argument was the main structural bull case. It is 40% weaker than I said.
claims.note: The underlying SIP series is still CONTESTED: Rs31,961cr vs Rs22,908cr, unresolved.

claims.claim: Conversion of announced capex into actual fixed assets fell from ~40% pre-2011 to 10-15%
claims.obtained: agent research, resolved a three-series contradiction
claims.why_load_bearing: Resolves why announced-capex headlines and actual-investment data disagree. It is the reason L&T-type exposure is a contract-mix question, not a headline question.

claims.claim: India's SPR covers 9.5 days (RTI, March 2026), against an IEA 90-day standard; one-third of facilities empty
claims.why_load_bearing: Determines how much an oil shock actually hurts. The 9.5 vs 60 vs 74 spread is a definitional gap: caverns-only versus mandated refiner stock.
claims.note: Partially resolved -- methodology explains the gap. Not fully closed.

claims.claim: RBI FX reserves are rising, not depleting
claims.obtained: agent research against the WSS series
claims.why_load_bearing: I had assumed depletion. Reserves rising removes one leg of the currency-crisis framing.
claims.note: News figures and the WSS series disagree on the SAME date. Use WSS.

claims.claim: The US is now India's largest remittance source at 27.7%
claims.why_load_bearing: A core strand of the Washington-concentration finding. Remittances were the channel I had assumed was diversified away from the US.

claims.claim: FPI outflows Rs2.87 lakh crore YTD 2026 as of 25 June; net FDI near a record low of $7.65bn against record gross FDI of $95bn
claims.why_load_bearing: Net versus gross FDI is the whole story -- record gross with near-record-low net means repatriation, which reads as an exit, not an entry.

claims.claim: Goods trade deficit $30.43bn in June 2026 (+59.3% YoY), $31.98bn in July, a 6-month high; current account back to a $6.2bn deficit in June
claims.why_load_bearing: The external position is deteriorating while the equity market treats India as a domestic story.

claims.claim: EU CBAM: 15-22% price hit on steel, 41% drop in aluminium exports, $116/tonne by 2034; the India-EU FTA does NOT exempt India
claims.why_load_bearing: An India-EU FTA headline will be read as bullish for metals. It is not, and this is why.

claims.claim: 199 forged Tejas supplier test certificates found by HAL's own audit; 18 fighters with 10 engineless by April 2026; only 7 GE engines delivered against a $1bn deal
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the HAL position. If the certificate count is wrong the close was still right on the engine number alone, so the decision is robust to this one being off.

claims.claim: MSRDC Rs45cr differential-interest payment; RBI query into the board's own Rs1 lakh penalty on its CEO; US securities class action
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the MEDIUM and suspended the LONG. Three independent items pointing the same way is what made it decisive rather than any one of them.

claims.claim: Dixon Q1 FY27 operating margin 2.29%, down from 3.04% YoY; revenue +21.1%, operating income -8.6%, net income +194.8% at 1.86x operating income
claims.obtained: own pull of yfinance quarterly financials, computed here
claims.why_load_bearing: Closed the position. Settles the dixon-pat conflict: neither the -36% screen figure nor our +119% TTM figure described what was happening.
claims.note: Sep 2025 quarter missing from the series; does not affect the like-for-like comparison. NOT checked against a company filing.

claims.claim: Q1 FY27, 62 large Indian names: revenue-weighted operating income +1.6% and margin -207bps, but ex three operationally negative names (IOC, BPCL, TMPV) operating income +15.4% and margin -32bps; median company +20.3%, breadth 44/62
claims.obtained: own computation from yfinance quarterly financials
claims.why_load_bearing: Overturns a bearish economy-wide margin-collapse read that the aggregate alone supports. Establishes the standing rule that an Indian aggregate is never reported without its median and breadth.
claims.note: Three loss-makers are 26.6% of sample revenue with a combined operating loss of Rs7,776cr. Not comparable to the FY26 4.5% net figure -- different period, different measure, different universe.

claims.claim: S&P 500 translated to INR beat the Nifty in 97% of 108 rolling 10-year windows, 92% of 5-year and 72% of 3-year, mean gap ~4.5-4.8pp/yr; every calendar sub-period 2008-2026 favours the S&P in rupees
claims.obtained: own computation, 228 months of monthly data from 2007-09
claims.why_load_bearing: Undercuts the framing premise of this entire workspace. An India-specific book must clear a ~4.5pp/yr structural headwind versus a passive foreign alternative, and with 4 of 30 theses scored there is no evidence yet that it does.
claims.note: Not tested against an equal-weight or ex-mega-cap S&P, which is the obvious first challenge. 2023-2026 gap of +15.23pp is driven by US mega-cap concentration.

claims.claim: Every $10/bbl on crude widens India's CAD by ~$16.7bn (India Ratings) and adds ~60bp to inflation (CareEdge); crude sustained at $80 adds ~0.4pp CPI and 0.3-0.5% of GDP to the CAD (Moneycontrol)
claims.obtained: agent research, cross-checked against own computation
claims.why_load_bearing: Sizes every oil scenario for India. Independently confirms the $16-20bn/yr figure computed here from assumed 4.5-5.5 mb/d imports -- two methods, same answer.
claims.source: India Ratings via BW Businessworld 2026-03-31; CareEdge via ET 2026-03-30
claims.note: Own bottom-up estimate was $16-20bn per $10. India Ratings says $16.7bn. Agreement across independent methods.

claims.claim: The Russian crude discount fully eroded and inverted to a PREMIUM during 2026: Urals topped Brent in the Indian market for the first time (Reuters 2026-03-06), delivered Urals neared $100 (Mar), 'strong demand flips Russian Urals to premium' (2026-08-21)
claims.why_load_bearing: India is carrying the Senate-sanctions tail risk -- a 100% tariff threat that passed the Senate 86-11 -- for a discount that no longer exists. The strategic cost is being paid and the economic benefit is gone.
claims.note: No source gives a current $/bbl premium figure. Unresolved.

unresolved_conflicts.why_it_matters: The absorption maths uses this directly.

unresolved_conflicts.conflict: The $145bn total does not reconcile with the World Bank series ($83bn to $129bn, 2019-2023)
unresolved_conflicts.why_it_matters: Sizes the largest single stabilising inflow India has.
Three different numbers for the same quantity means at least two are wrong.
Immaterial to any decision. Logged so it stops being re-litigated.

unresolved_conflicts.conflict: RESOLVED (reasoned, not verified): 9.5 days = ISPRL strategic caverns only; ~60 days = refiner/OMC mandated rolling commercial stock; 74 days = the combined buffer the government cites. Not contradictory -- three different pools.
unresolved_conflicts.why_it_matters: Sizes the oil-shock buffer. Caverns were 64% full in March 2026 ('one-third empty').
unresolved_conflicts.status: CLOSED, reasoned -- no primary PIB or ISPRL document confirms the arithmetic
